figure.name: Eugene V. Debs
figure.role: American labor leader, socialist candidate, organizer, speaker, and prisoner for anti-war speech.
figure.hook: Debs = U.S. labor politics and American socialism.
whyHere: Debs belongs here because he brings the road into American democratic life: railroads, unions, strikes, elections, courts, prisons, and public speech.
He matters because socialism in the United States is not only a foreign scare-word. It also has a labor, free-speech, voting, and class-solidarity history.
figure.cleanIdea: Debs asks whether democracy can hear working people when wealth, courts, employers, and war pressure push the other way.

hallCard.timelineMeaning: Labor politics, elections, unions, railroads, prisons, and public speech bring socialist language into U.S. democratic life.

ideas.title: Unionism
ideas.plainDefinition: Unionism means workers organizing together to bargain, strike, vote, and force employers and government to hear them.
ideas.context: In the Debs path, unionism is the practical doorway from individual frustration to organized labor power.
ideas.whyMatters: Unionism matters because socialism in the United States often enters politics through labor organization, not abstract theory first.

ideas.title: American Socialism
ideas.plainDefinition: American socialism is the U.S. labor and electoral tradition that used socialist language for unions, democracy, public ownership debates, anti-war speech, and class politics.
ideas.context: In the Debs path, American socialism is not imported as a cartoon. It is part of U.S. labor and democratic history.
ideas.whyMatters: American socialism matters because it keeps the project from letting anti-communist shorthand erase U.S. labor history.

ideas.title: Labor Politics
ideas.plainDefinition: Labor politics means workers using unions, parties, strikes, campaigns, and public speech to change economic and political power.
ideas.context: In the Debs path, labor politics connects shop-floor conflict to elections and public argument.
ideas.whyMatters: Labor politics matters because it shows democracy is not only voting. It is also the struggle over whether ordinary workers can organize power.
